# Gospel of Thomas, Saying 1 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Nag Hammadi Codex II, p. 32 | **Source Image:** source-texts/coptic/GTH_001_page_001.jpg

---

## Prologue and Saying 1

**1** These are the hidden [ехнт / hidden, secret] words [шаже / words, sayings] that the living [оноз / living] Jesus [іhсоус] spoke [жоос] and Didymos [дідумос / Twin] Judas [іоудас] Thomas [θωμас] wrote down [сhч].

**2** And he said: "Whoever [петнаχε] finds [хе] the interpretation [херменеіа / interpretation, meaning] of these sayings [нейшаже] will not taste [натжі] death [мою]."

---

**Textual Notes (EMET):**
- *нетхп* (hidden/secret): root *хп*, concealed; cf. P.Oxy 654 ἀπόκρυφοι (hidden/secret)
- *шаже* (pl. *шажe*): word, saying, logion; rendered "words" in prologue per Coptic usage
- *оноз iiс*: "the living Jesus" — attributive adjective precedes noun in Coptic; cf. P.Oxy 654 Ἰη(σοῦ)ς ζῶν
- *Дідумос*: Greek loan-word, "twin"; Thomas itself is Aramaic for "twin" — double designation
- *херменеіа*: Greek loan-word; "interpretation" (not merely "meaning" — implies active hermeneutical work)
- *натжі гоу мою*: literally "will not taste death" — idiom for escaping mortality; cf. John 8:52
